tools.description: Load onboarding context for this session: who the user is, the org and project profiles, memories, recent changes, skills. Use ONCE at the start of a task.
tools.name: context

tools.description: List projects in the organization, including the user's personal project. Pass a project's name or id as `scope` to knowledge_base and knowledge_base_write, or as `project` to research, wiki_stats and wiki_graph. Results come one page at a time: the result's coverage says whether more exist, and passing its next_cursor as cursor returns the next page.
tools.name: list_projects

tools.description: Ask a question and get a researched, cited answer from the organization's knowledge base, documents and connected services. The primary tool for questions about the organization: decisions, owners, status, everything related to a topic. Pass the user's original wording and scope; add context separately. Do not turn a natural-language criterion into a requirement for an exact field or taxonomy label. For counts, averages and all/none claims, inspect checked/not_checked and coverage: citations support evidence, not complete population coverage. Resolve material gaps before presenting a result as exhaustive. Pass quick=true for a short cited answer within 15 seconds from one search of Knowledge and documents (no connected services): for checking a fact before going on, not for exhaustive questions.
tools.name: research

tools.description:
Read the knowledge base: the commands Beakr's in-product agents use. Pass the command as `command` and its options as a flat `arguments` object; `scope` (a project name or id) narrows the read to one project. There is no `search` command.

Find, then walk the graph instead of re-searching or grepping the documents (every document, its date and matter are already indexed):
- sections: START HERE for a fact, value, decision or status (semantic; top 10 sections, each with the verbatim passage it rests on: quote it). [DISPUTED] marks a snippet a later source contradicts. grep: literal ids and exact names, not a census (output_mode files_with_matches lists every page with a term).
- Records (a matter, deal, study) are pages whose children are their documents and whose links name their parties, instruments and filings. hover {page} or cat {page, outline} shows those edges; follow them. cat reads narrowly (section_id, lines).
- Latest or largest: rows {table: facts, page_type, attribute, order_by: when or value, descending} ranks every record; cat the top few, then their children for the executed documents.
- Every record with a party or instrument: rows {table: connections, to} or links {page, page_type, relation}. How many: ls {page_type} (whole population, after_title), then check each. rows is every card as one table (filter, sort, group_by for counts); 0 rows means no card states it under that name, not that it is absent.
- One record: ls {parent}, links {page, direction: out}, timeline {page}.
- provenance, blame: support for a claim; log, diff, show: change over time only; proposals: your pending writes.
Exact wording: sources {page} lists every cited passage; read_file with a citation's reference (memo.pdf › p. 7), a file id or a path opens the original there. Slack, email, calendar and Jira items are not files: use their excerpt and url.
Results stay under about 6k tokens; when `next` appears, page with it rather than re-querying. In a code cell (Codex), print only the result's text and make one knowledge_base call per cell.
Citations read (memo.pdf › p. 7): read_file opens one, a write cites it as reference; cite people the same way, linked when there is a url. Full guidance: command='help' (`topic`: one command).

Command index (options go in `arguments`):
Find pages: sections {query, page_type?, limit?} (START HERE); grep {query, mode?, output_mode?, after_title?, context_lines?, matches_per_page?, limit?} (mode: text, regex, semantic, history; output_mode: content, files_with_matches, count: listings give the exact total, paged by after_title, where results say 'in their prose'); ls {parent?, page_type?, sort_by?, limit?} (sort_by: title|updated_at|created_at).
Read: cat {page, section_id?, lines?, outline?, rev?} (prefer section_id from a hit); hover {page} (its edges and summary: cheap triage before cat).
Graph: links {page, direction? (in|out), page_type?, relation?, limit?, offset?}; references {page}; timeline {page?, timeline_query?, start_date?, end_date?, include_content?, include_approx?, cursor?}; rows {table: facts|connections|findings, page_type?, entity?, to?, attribute?, query?, start_date?, end_date?, current_only?, order_by?, descending?, limit?, offset?, include_evidence?, group_by?, regex?, view?, field_id?} (to: connections involving a page; view: fields lists field names in use); ontology {include_proposed?}; suggest_parent {page | title, content?}.
Trust and lineage: provenance {page}; blame {page}; sources {page}.
History: log {page?}; diff {page, rev, rev2?}; show {page, rev}.
Utility: diagnostics {}; completions {prefix}; proposals {status?}; help {topic?}.
`page` accepts a slug, title, UUID or citation key such as wiki:8f3a0c21. Each result ends with its Sources: per cited document, its path, every place cited in it (p. 7, slide 3, sheet 2, B4:D9), the id read_file opens and its source_ref. Cite with the readable reference, to people and in writes (reference), or with the source_ref.
tools.name: knowledge_base

tools.description:
Propose a knowledge-base change through the actions Beakr's in-product agents use. Nothing is written until accept_proposal, unless the result says the user's auto-approve is on. Pass the action as `action` and its fields as a flat `arguments` object; every change except page_type needs `rationale`. Read the page first.

Choosing an action:
- edit_section: PREFERRED for updates. Replaces ONE section's whole body (its ### headings included) and leaves the rest of the page and its citations alone; a missing section_id plus title creates the section (after= positions it).
- edit: patches for surgical changes; `sections` REPLACES the whole page (an omitted section is deleted; keep a section's id to keep its citations and links).
- new: title, page_type, summary and `sections`; do not author section markers.
- add_fact, add_connection, add_finding: one row or one dated finding on a map card, merged into the live table -- never resend a table. Facts are what a source says; your conclusions are findings. edit_rows changes, merges or deletes rows; sort_table orders a table. A card's Facts, Connections and Findings rows are PROTECTED: only these actions change them, and an edit_section, edit or find_replace that would is refused.
- find_replace: batched replacements across one project (renames, links).
- mv within a project; copy to another (scope is the target); archive.
- merge: for a DUPLICATE page -- prefer it over archive so links keep resolving; name the duplicate's sections to keep in merge_sections.
- flag: ask a person to decide (ambiguity, contradiction, unverifiable, likely_error); writes nothing.
- page_type: only when no existing type fits.
When to write: after a cited answer the organization will want again, propose what you established. A sourced value is add_fact (reuse the attribute names knowledge_base rows view=fields lists, so it sits beside the rest); a relation is add_connection, on the more specific card; your conclusion is add_finding (about: the pages it bears on; supersedes: the finding it replaces). An out-of-date value is not deleted: add the newer dated row. Skip one-off analysis and personal preferences.
Full guidance for every action: action='help', or action='help' with `topic` set to one action.

Action index (fields go in `arguments`):
edit_section {page, section_id, new_section_body, citations?} (PREFERRED for updates); add_fact {page, attribute, value, evidence, when?}; add_connection {page, relation, to, evidence, when?}; add_finding {page, date, kind, text, evidence}; edit_rows; sort_table; new {title, page_type, summary, sections, parent?}; edit {page, patches | sections}; find_replace; mv; archive; merge; copy; page_type.
`sections` is an ordered list of {title, body, citations?}; Beakr writes the section markers. Citations are {reference | source_ref, stance, meta?}: reference the readable reference a read prints (memo.pdf › p. 7, #deals › message 2026-03-04 14:02 UTC, Page Title › Section), source_ref one from a Sources line; stance is support, qualifies or contradicts. In a body, cite a claim inline with the reference in parentheses as a read prints it (memo.pdf › p. 7): Beakr stores it as that citation. Cite your conversation as {key: conversation:<label>, source_type: conversation, source_title, meta: {excerpt}} and {{conversation:<label>}} after the claim. Cite only your conversation, a file you uploaded, or a source Knowledge already cites that you can read; anything else is refused (citation_not_citeable).
tools.name: knowledge_base_write

tools.description: Read a file's text (PDF, Word, sheet, slides, text, or a canvas): the original a Knowledge citation points at. Use when you need the exact wording or a value the excerpt does not hold. Pass `artifact_id`: the file id (`read_file <id>` in a result's Sources, or location.file_id), a version id, a citation's reference (memo.pdf › p. 7), or the file's path from a Sources line (deals/x/Closing/memo.docx). Add ' › <unit>' (memo.pdf › p. 7, book.xlsx › sheet 2, B4:D9, notes.md › lines 10-30) to get the window around that place. Connected items (Slack, email, calendar, Jira) are not stored as files: use their excerpt and url. Long files come back in pieces: pass `offset` to continue.
tools.name: read_file

tools.description: List the user's Beakr skills, or read one skill's SKILL.md (pass a slug, name or id). Use before a task a skill may cover. Results come one page at a time: the result's coverage says whether more exist, and passing its next_cursor as cursor returns the next page.
tools.name: skills

tools.description: See what Knowledge agents are working on right now in one project (or label): who is planning to read or change which pages, and what is waiting. Use before a large Knowledge write to avoid colliding with another agent's work in progress. The result's coverage says whether everything was shown, and next says how to narrow it when it was not.
tools.name: workboard

tools.description: Find Beakr tools beyond the ones listed: proposals review, profile lookups, knowledge base statistics, past conversations, imports, the audit log, and Beakr's version and update. Pass `search` to filter by name or description, or nothing to see them all. Each result gives the tool's name, description and input schema; call it by that name.
tools.name: discover_tools

tools.description: Search original indexed file text with command='grep', find passages by meaning with 'search', read a line window with 'read', or browse files with 'ls'. grep for exact wording and every file that mentions a term; search when you do not know the words (a concept or paraphrase): it ranks passages, grouped by document, with a match label and each file's source_ref, file_id and version_id, and is a ranked selection, not a census. Pass command options in arguments and a project ID or name in project. grep accepts pattern, output_mode (content, files_with_matches, count), path/glob, head_limit, offset and after_document; search takes query, limit, offset, passages and path/glob; read takes document and start_line/end_line. Check scan notices: offset pages matches already found; after_document resumes a partial scan. Unindexed files are not searched. Download a file with POST /v1/artifacts/download-url and its source_ref. Requires the documents_api feature; if unavailable use research or read_file.
tools.name: documents

tools.description: Get the knowledge profile for the org or a project: goals, focus areas, core people, organizations and topics, and extraction guidance.
tools.name: get_profile

tools.description: Show knowledge base statistics (page count, source count).
tools.name: wiki_stats

tools.description: Summarize the knowledge graph: the most connected pages and basic stats. Use knowledge_base command='links' to explore one page's neighborhood. The result's coverage says whether everything was shown, and next says how to narrow it when it was not.
tools.name: wiki_graph

tools.description: Show one wiki proposal before accepting or dismissing it.
tools.name: show_proposal

tools.description: Accept and apply a wiki proposal. Only after the user explicitly asks to accept this specific proposal.
tools.name: accept_proposal

tools.description: Dismiss a wiki proposal after the user asks to reject it.
tools.name: dismiss_proposal

tools.description: Search your past conversations: sessions imported from Claude Code, Codex or ChatGPT, and your Beakr chats. Use when the user refers to earlier work or before redoing a task another session may have worked through. With a query it searches each conversation's index (title, summary, the entities and pages it touched); without one it lists your most recent imported sessions. Not for org knowledge: research and knowledge_base cover that. Results come one page at a time: the result's coverage says whether more exist, and passing its next_cursor as cursor returns the next page.
tools.name: conversations_search

tools.description: Save an agent session into the user's private Beakr conversations. To add to a session imported before, send only the new messages with base_index set to how many were imported before; without base_index the messages are read as the whole session.
tools.name: import_conversation

tools.description: Read the organization's audit trail (sign-ins, key and policy changes), newest first. Requires an organization admin. Pass `before` (an ISO time) to start further back; a next_cursor continues the list. Results come one page at a time: the result's coverage says whether more exist, and passing its next_cursor as cursor returns the next page.
tools.name: org_audit_log

tools.description: Report Beakr's version and whether a newer beakr-cli release exists. On the beakr CLI's local MCP server: the installed CLI version and the latest release. On the hosted MCP server: the server's version and the latest beakr-cli release the server knows of. Call when the user asks about the Beakr version or updates, or when a Beakr tool behaves as if it is out of date.
tools.name: beakr_version

tools.description: Update Beakr. Only call this when the user has asked to update Beakr; it takes no arguments. On the beakr CLI's local MCP server it upgrades the beakr-cli package with the tool that installed it (uv or pipx) and refreshes its installed skills; the running server keeps the old code, so tell the user to restart Claude Code / Codex afterwards. The hosted MCP server cannot change the user's machine: it runs nothing and returns the command to run locally instead (`beakr update`, or the install command when the CLI is not installed).
tools.name: update_beakr
